names.legendary: Fellgrim, Cleaver of the Ancient Oak

lore.common: Gets stuck in the first log it meets. Insists the log is holding it hostage.
lore.uncommon: Splits firewood with one swing, then demands applause from the entire woodshed.
lore.rare: Whispers the secret weak point of every tree it touches. Lumberjacks adore it; the trees have hired security.
lore.epic: Brought down a colossal dead tree with a single swing, revealing an entire forgotten village inside its hollow trunk. The villagers asked it to put the roof back.
lore.legendary: Fellgrim was forged from a fallen star to sever the roots of an endless winter. Its blade can split a mountain's shadow without touching the mountain itself.

names.legendary: Velocipede, Rider of the Still Road

lore.common: Wears three jackets, two scarves and a towel. Has never needed a saddle.
lore.uncommon: Promises a mountain ride while its screen displays the same suspicious cow.
lore.rare: Steals one minute from every workout and spends it watching motivational videos.
lore.epic: Pedalled so furiously on New Year's Day that every bike in the gym joined in. By February they had all returned to holding washing.
lore.legendary: An ancient rider travelled the circumference of the Earth without leaving the spare room. Velocipede kept the road turning beneath him and sent postcards from every imaginary country.

names.legendary: Sweepella, Witch of the Wandering Wind

lore.common: Leaves one perfectly straight line of dust no matter how many times it sweeps.
lore.uncommon: Sheds so many bristles that every cleaning session ends dirtier than it began.
lore.rare: Catches cobwebs out of reach and relocates their spiders to more luxurious ceilings.
lore.epic: Swept the entire town square into one neat pile, including three bicycles, a mayor and a very confused statue.
lore.legendary: Sweepella once swept the autumn leaves out of the sky before they fell. The wind still chases her, demanding its leaves back.

names.legendary: Saint Slick of the Thousand Hinges

lore.common: Has an aim like a sleepy watering can. The squeaky hinge remains entirely unbothered.
lore.uncommon: Leaves tiny oily footprints beneath the workbench and blames the family bicycle.
lore.rare: Persuades rusty gates to open for visitors they actually like. Unwelcome salespeople hear a dramatic creak.
lore.epic: Silenced every door in the castle during a burglary drill. The guards now knock on walls to check whether they're still there.
lore.legendary: An ancient oil can whose single golden drop freed the drawbridge of a besieged city. The gates swung open, and an entire army marched into the wrong courtyard.

names.legendary: Tintora, Keeper of the First Colour

lore.common: Glued its lid shut during the night, then watches the decorator wrestle it at breakfast.
lore.uncommon: Leaves a permanent coloured tear down its side and insists it is modern art.
lore.rare: Looks blue in the tin, purple in daylight and alarmingly green under the kitchen lamp.
lore.epic: Tumbled down the school corridor, painting a different colour on every wall as it bounced. Parents called it the finest renovation in decades.
lore.legendary: Tintora kept the very first pigment in a sealed tin beneath a forgotten city. A single drop restored the faded murals of an entire palace, and the painted heroes stepped forward to thank her.

names.legendary: Bellgor, Judge of the Final Lift

lore.common: Rolls beneath the sofa whenever exercise is mentioned.
lore.uncommon: Adds a mysterious extra kilogram each time someone looks in the mirror.
lore.rare: Can make even a bodybuilder grunt like a dying accordion. The gym has banned it from quiet hours.
lore.epic: Challenged an entire gym to one final set. By dawn, the treadmills had fled and the mirrors were asking for sick leave.
lore.legendary: Bellgor was forged from the iron of a fallen mountain. It weighs only as much as the lifter's courage, which explains why no king has ever managed to move it.

names.legendary: Bangsworth, Architect of the Last Nail

lore.common: Never misses the chance to introduce itself to a thumb. The thumb does not reciprocate.
lore.uncommon: Bends every nail into a question mark. Considers this a contribution to philosophy.
lore.rare: Pulls nails from old walls so neatly that the pictures run away before they fall.
lore.epic: Struck the first blow on a new palace and woke every sleeping mountain. The builders had to apologise to the echoes.
lore.legendary: Bangsworth built a bridge from one side of a river to the other using a single golden nail. Every spring the bridge hums with the sound of that first strike.

names.legendary: Helmoria, Shield of the Endless Road

lore.common: Gets its chin strap tangled in absolutely everything except a chin.
lore.uncommon: Leaves strange little stripes in your hair. It considers this a heroic hairstyle.
lore.rare: Bounces off every doorway while protecting its owner from the owner's own lack of spatial awareness.
lore.epic: Rolled through a bicycle race collecting every fallen rider like a tiny armoured rescue wagon. Nobody was allowed to refuse a lift.
lore.legendary: Forged from the first fallen star, Helmoria guards any traveller brave enough to ride. Not even the mountain winds can unseat her crest.

names.legendary: Hydromina, Crown of the Silent Lanes

lore.common: Tugs one stray hair with the precision of a very tiny villain.
lore.uncommon: Squeaks against the forehead and refuses to sit straight for team photographs.
lore.rare: Turns any swimmer into a sleek underwater dart; their ears make the sound of a tiny submarine.
lore.epic: Shot through all eight pool lanes in one dive, dragging the starting blocks into a spectacular whirlpool.
lore.legendary: Hydromina was woven from the skin of the first wave and never lets a drop slow her bearer. The pool stays perfectly still until she passes.

names.legendary: Amphitron, Lord of Land and Lagoon

lore.common: Rolls into ponds without checking whether its passengers wanted a swim. They never do.
lore.uncommon: Has wheels on Monday and a propeller on Tuesday. Its identity crisis is everybody else's sightseeing tour.
lore.rare: Climbs waterfalls on its tyres and offers confused salmon a lift. All fares must be paid in bubbles.
lore.epic: Drove a passenger bus through the harbour and emerged towing a lost pirate ship. The pirates demanded to know where the next stop was.
lore.legendary: Amphitron can drive across oceans and sail over mountains, turning rivers into roads beneath its wheels. The world's mapmakers have started drawing routes in pencil.

names.legendary: Aurebrass, Keeper of Names in Gold

lore.common: Turns green the week after polishing. It calls the effect an antique finish.
lore.uncommon: Insists its name be engraved on every park bench. Nobody knows who ordered the signs.
lore.rare: Reflects sunlight so brightly that people finally stop to read the dedication nobody usually notices.
lore.epic: Flashed from a polished memorial plaque with such force that the bakery across the road toasted every bun at once. The plaque received a thank-you card.
lore.legendary: Aurebrass remembers names carved into metal after the world forgets their owners. On quiet evenings, each shining letter tells one small story.

names.legendary: Spirathor, Keeper of the Unwound Storm

lore.common: Springs from a dismantled pen and vanishes beneath furniture. Has never been recaptured.
lore.uncommon: Wraps itself around anything cylindrical, including the cat's tail. The cat disagrees with the plan.
lore.rare: Stores a thunderclap inside every turn. One bounce can knock the pictures off a wall.
lore.epic: Burst from a clock tower and uncoiled across the city, winding every street into a spiral. The tram drivers requested a new map.
lore.legendary: Spirathor binds the storm inside an endless metal helix. Legend says that if it ever straightens completely, time itself will lose its spring and every alarm clock will finally shut up.

names.legendary: Hookarius, Keeper of the Hanging City

lore.common: Grabs the sleeve of anyone passing by, then pretends it was just trying to say hello.
lore.uncommon: Keeps every winter coat in a tangled mountain until nobody can find the door.
lore.rare: Catches falling objects in midair, including a runaway hat and one extremely surprised umbrella.
lore.epic: Held up the entire town's winter coats during the festival. The wall collapsed under the weight of fashionable scarves.
lore.legendary: Hookarius was forged to hang the keys of an ancient city above its gates. No thief could reach them, and the people never locked their doors again.

names.legendary: Knottilda, the Neverending Tangle

lore.common: Ties your shoelaces together at the exact moment the bus arrives.
lore.uncommon: Pulls itself tighter whenever someone says this should be easy.
lore.rare: Can hold an entire ship at anchor, but deliberately unties the bathroom dressing gown.
lore.epic: Bound every contestant's shoelaces together at the school sports day, turning the sprint into a single enormous three-legged race.
lore.legendary: Knottilda once tied the beginning and end of a sailor's rope together so firmly that the ship sailed in circles for seven years. The crew now lives on an island shaped like a bow.

names.legendary: Grandmother Grindella, Witch of One Seed

lore.common: Thumps its pestle on the counter like a tiny drum, usually during somebody's phone call.
lore.uncommon: Turns three peppercorns into a fragrant cloud and pretends it's wearing perfume.
lore.rare: Grinds pepper so fine the whole kitchen sneezes in unison. The clock has begun setting its time by the sound.
lore.epic: Crushed the village's entire spice harvest into one sneeze-inducing cloud. Nobody could pronounce the dinner menu for a week.
lore.legendary: Grindella crushed one enchanted seed in her mortar and woke the dormant gardens of a winter kingdom. She charges exactly one peppercorn for each spring.

names.legendary: Plectrion, Keeper of the Last Encore

lore.common: Falls through the guitar's sound hole and rattles until everyone stops playing.
lore.uncommon: Carves a tiny signature into the guitar after every song. Nobody can read the handwriting.
lore.rare: Strums a riff that the guitarist has not yet learned, then waits impatiently for them to catch up.
lore.epic: Leaped between every guitar at the festival and played a roaring solo without a single musician touching a string.
lore.legendary: Plectrion vanished into the crowd after a legendary final concert. Fifty years later it returned to the same guitar, carrying one unwritten melody that made the audience sing again.

names.legendary: Planorax, Sculptor of the First Forest

lore.common: Produces curly wood shavings that get into everyone's hair. Claims they are free wigs.
lore.uncommon: Fixes a sticky door by shaving off just enough wood to make it fit every other doorway instead.
lore.rare: Turns wooden furniture perfectly smooth with one stroke. The cat now slides off the sofa.
lore.epic: Shaved a thousand planks at once and filled the whole village with a swirling blizzard of sawdust curls.
lore.legendary: Planorax shaped the first trees from raw mountains. To this day, every perfectly flat plank is a stolen piece of ancient wilderness, and the forests want their corners back.

names.legendary: Terracotta, Mother of a Thousand Pots

lore.common: Spins clay into a crooked mug, then presents it as an artistic choice.
lore.uncommon: Wobbles just enough to make every vase grow a suspiciously large ear.
lore.rare: Spins an ordinary lump of earth into a perfect bowl that whispers the recipe for its own glaze.
lore.epic: Revolved through a pottery workshop and sculpted every visitor into a clay statue. They kept their hats, somehow.
lore.legendary: Terracotta once shaped an entire city from river mud on a single turning wheel. At dawn the streets hardened, and the residents still hear her humming beneath them.

names.legendary: Reelith, Spinner of the Seven Tides

lore.common: Tangles its line into a knot so complicated that the fish stop to admire it.
lore.uncommon: Clicks a little faster every time an angler boasts about the one that got away.
lore.rare: Winds a hooked fish to shore before the fish realises it has swallowed the bait.
lore.epic: Spun so fiercely it reeled an entire fishing pier across the harbour. The anglers had to buy new tickets for the return trip.
lore.legendary: Reelith cast a line across seven seas to retrieve a pearl lost beneath the deepest trench. Its silver spool still sings whenever a storm approaches.

names.legendary: Old Flashbell, the Pier's Last Performer

lore.common: Swallows a token and offers a tinny fanfare instead of a prize.
lore.uncommon: Flashes its lights for the seagulls after the arcade has closed for the night.
lore.rare: Spins its symbols into a message only the pier's retired caretaker understands.
lore.epic: Woke every silent amusement machine on the pier at midnight. Their jingling concert brought the seaside ghosts back for one last dance.
lore.legendary: Old Flashbell performed beneath the boardwalk's lamps for a century, long after everyone forgot its name. On winter nights it lights the empty pier so lost visitors can find the shore.

names.legendary: Spinella, Needle of Unwritten Destinies

lore.common: Spins happily until one strand of wool turns into a knot with opinions.
lore.uncommon: Winds stray fluff into a tiny scarf and presents it to the cat.
lore.rare: Spins thread strong enough to stitch a torn sail during a storm, yet fine enough to pass through a raindrop.
lore.epic: Wound every loose thread at the craft fair into one enormous rope, which promptly tied the entire village into an accidental maypole dance.
lore.legendary: Spinella spins the thread that holds forgotten stories together. Cut her silver yarn and every fairy tale suddenly needs a new ending.

names.legendary: Aetherella, the Endless Swing

lore.common: Squeaks on the way up and demands applause on the way down.
lore.uncommon: Pinches sleeves in its chains, then shouts higher with every creak.
lore.rare: Pauses at the very highest point for a whole minute, giving its rider a view across every rooftop.
lore.epic: Swung over the playground so high it snagged a cloud and dragged a thunderstorm into the sandpit.
lore.legendary: Aetherella carries the final push given by a parent long ago. Each evening an empty swing rises gently so another child can feel that impossible moment of flight.

names.legendary: Aerion, the Featherless Albatross

lore.common: Blocks the passenger's perfect mountain photograph with its enormous elbow.
lore.uncommon: Flexes its flaps before landing like a nervous bird practising a bow.
lore.rare: Guides lost migrating birds along its wake, making a silver highway through turbulent clouds.
lore.epic: Stormcleaver Roc stretched across a hurricane and carved one calm flight path straight through its eye. The storm issued a complaint about trespassing.
lore.legendary: Aerion learned to fly without ever flapping. Generations of geese follow his metal shadow across the oceans, and every autumn he returns them safely to the same marsh.

names.legendary: Tallis, the Stairway to Storms

lore.common: Smacks its owner's shins while being carried through the narrowest doorway.
lore.uncommon: Adds a wobbly rung whenever somebody boasts about not being afraid of heights.
lore.rare: Reaches the roof even when nobody remembers buying such a tall ladder.
lore.epic: Grew through the top of the town hall while the painters weren't looking. The mayor was last seen polishing the weather vane above the clouds.
lore.legendary: Tallis was built to reach the sky when the first thunderstorm refused to pass. Its highest rung still touches the storm's doorstep, where lightning knocks before entering the world.

names.legendary: Mowzart, Maestro of the Green

lore.common: Needs exactly eleven pulls of the starter cord, and only accepts the twelfth from a neighbour.
lore.uncommon: Packs the grass box so full that it starts leaving clippings behind in neat little gifts.
lore.rare: Mows perfect stripes into a lawn even when the grass has decided to grow sideways.
lore.epic: Started before dawn on the quietest Sunday of the year and mowed every garden in the neighbourhood. The entire street formed a committee.
lore.legendary: Mowzart cuts the royal gardens into patterns visible from the stars. One night it trimmed the grass into a score of music, and the wind played it as the sun rose.

names.legendary: Mophelia, Thirst of the Seven Seas

lore.common: Pushes the spilled water into a bigger puddle first. Claims the detour is important.
lore.uncommon: Squirts the cleaner with a revenge splash whenever somebody twists its head.
lore.rare: Polishes tiles so brightly that the kitchen doubles as an ice rink. The dog is furious.
lore.epic: Drank a flood from the town hall in one enormous gulp. The mayor gave it a medal before it sneezed the water over everyone at the ceremony.
lore.legendary: Mophelia absorbed the waters of a drowned city, saving its libraries and bakeries alike. Each year it wrings one tear into the harbour, and the tide rises to say thank you.

names.legendary: Master Bristleo, Weaver of Horizons

lore.common: Sheds one bristle into every freshly painted wall, like an extremely tiny autograph.
lore.uncommon: Carries a bright drip down its handle until it reaches the painter's elbow.
lore.rare: Paints the eyes of portraits so well that they blink when the gallery closes.
lore.epic: Painted a door on a blank brick wall and the entire school marched through it before anyone checked where it led.
lore.legendary: Master Bristleo painted a bridge across an impossible ravine using only moonlight and three strokes of silver. At dawn it became real, and two divided villages met in its middle.

names.legendary: Gripmother, Unbender of Ancient Locks

lore.common: Pinches the one screw that is already loose and lets it ping under the cabinet.
lore.uncommon: Twists copper wire into tiny metal birds that perch on the toolbox.
lore.rare: Opens rusted locks and knots of iron with one squeeze, then complains about its aching handles.
lore.epic: Gripped the chain anchoring a runaway bridge and hauled it back across the river. The villagers offered it a handshake at their own risk.
lore.legendary: Gripmother freed the gates of an ancient city when their iron hinges had fused after centuries. One mighty squeeze opened the road home to a lost generation.

names.legendary: Shearadon, Sculptor of Living Mazes

lore.common: Spits clippings into its owner's hair and calls them decorative confetti.
lore.uncommon: Cuts a perfectly straight line until someone says looking good. Then it veers into a zigzag.
lore.rare: Turns an ordinary hedge into an impossibly convincing green dragon. The neighbour's cat has moved house.
lore.epic: Sculpted the entire town's hedges into a giant maze before lunch. The council meeting lasted three days because nobody found the hall.
lore.legendary: Shearadon shaped a forest into living statues that move only when the moon rises. The oldest sculpture is a gardener, still holding a pair of hedge clippers.

names.legendary: Boreas Blower, Lord of the Last Leaf

lore.common: Starts at seven on Saturday morning because the neighbours need an alarm clock.
lore.uncommon: Moves leaves from one garden into another, then acts shocked when they return.
lore.rare: Whips a pile of autumn leaves into a swirling miniature hurricane.
lore.epic: Launched three garden gnomes, a wheelbarrow and the mayor's hat across the park while trying to clear the footpath. The hat landed first.
lore.legendary: Boreas Blower summoned a wind strong enough to strip the autumn colour from an entire forest in one breath. By the next morning every leaf had landed in a perfect golden spiral around one stubborn oak.

names.legendary: Drillgorath, Eater of Mountains

lore.common: Chews the plaster beside the screw hole and calls the mess precision work.
lore.uncommon: Growls like an angry wasp whenever the battery reaches one percent.
lore.rare: Burrows through brick and steel, leaving perfect tunnels that small mice immediately rent.
lore.epic: Dug through three adjoining houses while installing a single shelf. The neighbours now share a hallway and a very complicated mortgage.
lore.legendary: Drillgorath carved the first mountain pass with one diamond-tipped tooth. It still demands a fresh drill bit whenever travellers cross.

names.legendary: Thatchor, Harvester of the Last Leaves

lore.common: Lies with its teeth upward and waits for a careless foot. Boink is its battle cry.
lore.uncommon: Makes a perfect leaf pile, then guards it like the world's worst treasure.
lore.rare: Scrapes every patch of moss from the lawn, exposing buried coins and three annoyed worms.
lore.epic: Pulled all the autumn leaves into one gigantic mound in the town square. Children disappeared inside it for a week and came out wearing crowns.
lore.legendary: Thatchor gathered an entire forest's autumn leaves into one mountain-sized heap. The hedgehogs declared it a sovereign nation.

names.legendary: Sawbella, Carver of Kingdoms

lore.common: Sings an awful squeaky tune with every stroke, and the wood joins in unwillingly.
lore.uncommon: Makes a pile of sawdust large enough to hide a suspiciously guilty squirrel.
lore.rare: Cuts through timber so neatly that the two halves wait until the carpenter looks away before falling apart.
lore.epic: Chewed through the castle drawbridge during repairs and built a new staircase from the pieces before the knights could complain.
lore.legendary: Sawbella carved an entire settlement from one enchanted tree without wasting a splinter. Its wood still grows new doors whenever the village welcomes a stranger.

names.legendary: Sir Slotwell, Twister of the Locked Door

lore.common: Is flat-headed whenever the job needs a cross. It thinks this is hilarious.
lore.uncommon: Slips from a screw and leaves a shiny scratch on the brand-new cabinet.
lore.rare: Can open any stubborn paint can with one twist, though nobody remembers why that is its special talent.
lore.epic: Assembled a thousand flatpack wardrobes in one night. By sunrise the furniture shop had become an intricate wooden maze.
lore.legendary: Sir Slotwell unscrewed the door to a forgotten library without breaking its ancient lock. Behind it lay a thousand unfinished stories, and he has been turning their pages ever since.

names.legendary: Shovald, Underworld Cartographer

lore.common: Carries more mud home on its blade than it ever moves out of the garden.
lore.uncommon: Discovers buried dog toys instead of potatoes and insists that is a better harvest.
lore.rare: Digs a tunnel beneath the hedge to reveal the mole's secret underground ballroom.
lore.epic: Excavated a complete Roman bath beneath the allotments in one afternoon. The gardeners immediately argued over who owned the towels.
lore.legendary: Shovald mapped the underground rivers that had no names and carved stairs down to their shores. The first explorers returned carrying lanternfish and a complaint about the lack of handrails.

names.legendary: Measurion, Surveyor of Forever

lore.common: Springs back into its case and nips anyone foolish enough to trust it.
lore.uncommon: Bends midway through measuring a shelf and produces a very confident wrong answer.
lore.rare: Changes a room's dimensions when nobody is looking. The sofa fit yesterday; today it needs a permit.
lore.epic: Unrolled itself around the royal palace and discovered it was three inches too short. The builders had to move a tower.
lore.legendary: Measurion walked the edge of the world with a steel measuring ribbon, marking every distance a traveller could dream. The final number was the length of a promise.

names.legendary: Fixalotl, the Walking Workshop

lore.common: Rattles so loudly in the car boot that the driver thinks the engine is falling off.
lore.uncommon: Counts its spanners at bedtime and accuses the hammer of stealing one.
lore.rare: Finds the one missing tool by sniffing out the screw it was meant to fit.
lore.epic: Opened itself in the middle of a ruined castle and rebuilt the battlements before the invading army could finish breakfast.
lore.legendary: Fixalotl has repaired the same clock tower every night for a thousand years, adding one impossible gear each visit. Nobody knows what the clock measures now, but the town has never lost a minute.

names.legendary: Ribbonia, Guardian of Lost Victories

lore.common: Twists itself so the medal hangs backward just as the photographer arrives.
lore.uncommon: Taps its medal against every button on the winner's shirt.
lore.rare: Makes its wearer's shoulders stand straighter, even when the race was only to the garden gate.
lore.epic: Tangled a hundred runners at the finish line into one giant victory necklace. The judges gave everyone first place.
lore.legendary: Ribbonia carried the medals of champions whose names were lost to time. Whenever courage is shown without a crowd, one silver thread in her weave begins to shine.

names.legendary: Aurelius, the Cup No Champion Could Keep

lore.common: Collects dust so quickly that its winner thinks it has grown fur.
lore.uncommon: Breaks a handle during every overenthusiastic victory speech.
lore.rare: Reflects the winning moment endlessly in its gold surface, even when the contest ended years ago.
lore.epic: Leapt from the trophy cabinet and challenged every previous champion to one enormous rematch. The school field needed extra seating.
lore.legendary: Aurelius has belonged to the finest champions of a hundred generations, yet vanishes whenever victory makes its holder cruel. It always returns to the one competitor who helped a rival finish.

names.legendary: Pipricus, Whistle of the Lost Trail

lore.common: Blows directly beside the ear of anyone foolish enough to lend it to a child.
lore.uncommon: Carries a tiny rattling pea that will not stop boasting.
lore.rare: Calls every dog in the park with one impossibly high note.
lore.epic: Summoned every lost hiker from the mountain trails to the same picnic spot. The sandwiches didn't stand a chance.
lore.legendary: Its clear note once crossed a winter pass where every voice was swallowed by snow. The rescuers followed it to a buried shelter and found everyone singing along.

names.legendary: Refereon, the Unappealable Note

lore.common: Blows precisely as a striker is about to score.
lore.uncommon: Declares offside when even the linesman has gone for a sandwich.
lore.rare: Finds a foul in every match, including a pigeon stealing a chip.
lore.epic: Stopped the national final so abruptly that the entire stadium froze mid-cheer. The ball continued rolling alone into the goal.
lore.legendary: Has ended a thousand legendary matches with one unarguable sound. Even thunder waits for its final note before making any more noise.

names.legendary: Barrowbaron, the One-Wheel Wonder

lore.common: Tips over at the exact moment a gardener says almost there.
lore.uncommon: Complains with one heroic squeak for every turn of its lonely wheel.
lore.rare: Carries a dozen squabbling gnomes across the vegetable patch without dropping one.
lore.epic: Raced every barrow at the village fair, leaving an enormous trail of compost that became the world's fastest-growing flowerbed.
lore.legendary: Carried the stones to rebuild a destroyed village one load at a time. The villagers plated its humble wheel in gold, but it still prefers a good muddy path.

names.legendary: Torquessa, Who Loosened the Mountain

lore.common: Slips off a bolt and bonks its owner on the elbow, then acts innocent.
lore.uncommon: Adjusts its jaws to fit any nut except the one the mechanic actually needs.
lore.rare: Tightens the loosest screw in a rattling machine from across the workshop with one sharp metallic click.
lore.epic: Ironjaw Torquebeast gripped the town clock's enormous axle and wound it back into motion. Unfortunately, every cuckoo appeared at once to celebrate.
lore.legendary: Torquessa found a single rusted bolt holding shut an ancient mountain gate. With one turn she opened the pass, releasing a spring breeze, a lost caravan and a very irritated goat.

names.legendary: Lord Diggory, Architect of the Tides

lore.common: Flings sand into whichever sandwich has the least sand in it. It calls this fairness.
lore.uncommon: Digs a moat around every sandcastle, including castles belonging to complete strangers.
lore.rare: Can dig a hole so deep the incoming tide arrives early to investigate.
lore.epic: Built a fortress along the entire beach before breakfast. The crabs demanded diplomatic recognition by lunchtime.
lore.legendary: Every castle made by a child still stands somewhere in Diggory's hidden kingdom beneath the dunes. He visits them after the tide goes out.

names.legendary: Torquelius, Last Fastener of the Ages

lore.common: Loses its nut the moment somebody drops it. Has filed for separation.
lore.uncommon: Rusts in place so firmly that three mechanics now live beside it.
lore.rare: Bolted the workshop bench to the wall and the wall to the bicycle. The bicycle is still technically roadworthy.
lore.epic: Held a collapsing bridge together while the builders argued over which spanner to use. It charged them by the hour.
lore.legendary: When the first stars were hung in the sky, Torquelius tightened the final bolt. His wrench has never moved, and neither has the night.

names.legendary: Sir Tenacious, the Last Pin Standing

lore.common: Wobbles for ten seconds after every throw. It enjoys suspense more than bowling.
lore.uncommon: Falls over whenever anyone laughs at the bowler. The referee suspects sympathy.
lore.rare: Can stand firm against a perfect strike, then topples if someone whispers BOO.
lore.epic: Refused to fall during a championship and forced the tournament to continue into next week. The spectators voted it most valuable player.
lore.legendary: Ten thousand legendary bowlers have tried to topple Sir Tenacious. He still stands at the end of the lane, polishing his tiny crown.

names.legendary: Sir Slitwick, Opener of Secrets

lore.common: Clicks its blade out whenever somebody says BE CAREFUL. It considers itself very funny.
lore.uncommon: Lives in the toolbox and secretly trims the cardboard dividers into tiny castles.
lore.rare: Slices packing tape so silently that parcels keep pretending they are still sealed.
lore.epic: Opened ten thousand moving boxes in one hour and revealed a complete second house made of discarded cardboard. The movers tried to charge extra.
lore.legendary: Slitwick can open any seal without disturbing its contents. Once he opened a royal secret so carefully that the king didn't realise it was public for twenty years.

names.legendary: Bungarok, Binder of the Unbound

lore.common: Is always one centimetre too short. It considers this a personal triumph.
lore.uncommon: Wraps itself around roof racks like a clingy octopus, then ties the hooks together.
lore.rare: Stretches across impossible distances but refuses to retract when somebody actually needs it.
lore.epic: Snapped back so fiercely it launched the entire holiday luggage onto the hotel's balcony. The family had not yet booked a room.
lore.legendary: Bungarok once held two drifting islands together through a century-long storm. The islands are still attached, but nobody dares ask what happens if the hook slips.

names.legendary: Cordonnix, Weaver of the Wired World

lore.common: Enters a drawer perfectly straight and leaves wearing six other cables like jewellery.
lore.uncommon: Has twelve connectors. None fits the phone in front of you.
lore.rare: Plugs the kettle into a game console and the lamp into a toaster. Nobody knows which device is winning.
lore.epic: Grew three new tangled heads whenever someone untied a knot. A whole IT department surrendered after fourteen minutes.
lore.legendary: Every wire in the kingdom passes through Cordonnix's coils. Once it sneezed, and the royal coronation streamed directly to the village bread maker.

names.legendary: Celestigond, Ferryman of Frost

lore.common: Sways gently until the nervous tourist grabs the rail. Then sways a little more.
lore.uncommon: Gives the mountain's best view exclusively to the one passenger who is afraid of heights.
lore.rare: Stops between stations to admire the clouds. Its passengers have begun selling postcards.
lore.epic: Lifted a regiment of skiers into the storm and returned with an entire choir of snowmen. The lift operator requested unpaid leave.
lore.legendary: Celestigond ferries lost climbers between mountains that touch only at dawn. Every ticket is one warm memory, and nobody asks what happens to the return fare.

names.legendary: Fetterax, Keeper of Broken Locks

lore.common: Rattles against a bicycle frame on every bump and considers this percussion.
lore.uncommon: Falls off the sprocket precisely halfway up the steepest hill.
lore.rare: Wraps itself around any unattended object. The picnic bench has been chained to a duck.
lore.epic: Stretched across an entire harbour and held two departing ships together. Neither captain wanted to be the first to say sorry.
lore.legendary: Fetterax forged the links that once held a mountain in place. Every chain in the world remembers its name, and every padlock sleeps with one eye open.

names.legendary: Chiselgrim, Carver of Forgotten Kings

lore.common: Turns one neat line into a shower of splinters. Calls it artistic freedom.
lore.uncommon: Flinches whenever a mallet appears. The hammer insists they're friends.
lore.rare: Carves wooden faces that change expressions when nobody watches. The workshop feels judged.
lore.epic: Struck a marble statue once, and every statue in the capital climbed down from its pedestal to demand better working conditions.
lore.legendary: Chiselgrim cuts names into mountains so history cannot forget them. The latest name belongs to a king who hasn't been born yet, and the royal family is deeply concerned.

names.legendary: Clamperion, Keeper of the Final Grip

lore.common: Pinches its own owner's finger and pretends it was holding something important.
lore.uncommon: Tightens a quarter turn whenever someone says that's probably enough.
lore.rare: Grips a piece of timber so fiercely it remembers the shape after being released.
lore.epic: Locked every workbench in the city into one colossal ring. The carpenters held their union meeting inside it.
lore.legendary: Clamperion once held the cracking bridge between two rival kingdoms until they signed a treaty. Three centuries later he is still holding it and asking if they're absolutely sure.

names.legendary: Vintorax, Key to the Sleeping Vines

lore.common: Twists into the cork, then immediately forgets which direction to turn.
lore.uncommon: Throws up its tiny arms in triumph before doing any actual work.
lore.rare: Can open sealed letters, locked diaries and stubborn jars by mistake.
lore.epic: Uncorked the royal wine cellar in one gesture, unleashing a flood that left the entire court speaking in expensive tasting notes.
lore.legendary: Legend says Vintorax drilled the first spiral staircase into a mountain so a thirsty giant could reach his vineyard. It still charges corkage.

names.legendary: Croquetor, Judge of the Royal Lawn

lore.common: Strikes a flower instead of the ball. Blames the flower.
lore.uncommon: Challenges lawn ornaments to tournaments and always loses to the flamingo.
lore.rare: Sends rival balls politely into a distant rosebush, then apologizes with terrifying sincerity.
lore.epic: Knocked every ball through every hoop in one almighty shot, and accidentally rearranged the duke's garden into a maze.
lore.legendary: Croquetor once defeated a king without moving from his chair. The ball travelled through seven kingdoms before returning to tap the royal ankle.

names.legendary: Fulcrumax, He Who Opens the Sealed

lore.common: Opens paint tins with the dignity of a tiny burglar.
lore.uncommon: Gets stuck underneath the crate it was supposed to open.
lore.rare: Can prise apart a secret door but cannot loosen the lid on a jam jar.
lore.epic: Opened the city's most secure vault to reveal one umbrella and a note saying Back in five minutes.
lore.legendary: When the gods sealed the oldest gate beneath the mountain, Fulcrumax found the one loose hinge. The gods now require a building permit for all divine doors.

names.legendary: Rainthroat, Voice of the Drowned Roofs

lore.common: Burps every time it rains. The neighbors think the house is haunted.
lore.uncommon: Eats leaves all autumn, then complains bitterly about indigestion.
lore.rare: Can redirect an entire storm through one pipe. Always chooses the flowerbeds.
lore.epic: Gushed so fiercely that a garden pond rose onto the roof. The goldfish began charging rent to the pigeons.
lore.legendary: When the first city wept beneath a hundred nights of rain, Rainthroat sang the flood safely down its stone veins. The streets still hum its tune in thunderstorms.

names.legendary: Orbitron, Emperor of Going Nowhere

lore.common: Walks for an hour every morning. Has never made it past the television.
lore.uncommon: Counts every swinging handle as a handshake and insists it has hundreds of friends.
lore.rare: Its display claims you crossed the Alps. The machine won't explain the souvenir cowbell.
lore.epic: The gym's ellipticals began a midnight march without moving an inch. By sunrise their riders had travelled to imaginary France and demanded croissants.
lore.legendary: Pedalled for a thousand years without advancing a centimetre. Orbitron now rules an empire of unfinished resolutions and has named its throne January Second.

names.legendary: Sir Letterbane of the Sealed Kingdom

lore.common: Opens bills neatly and birthday cards like a hungry badger.
lore.uncommon: Lives on the desk and insists the stapler address it as Your Sharpness.
lore.rare: Can slice through any sealed secret, except the office coffee budget.
lore.epic: Opened the entire government's backlog of correspondence in one stroke. Three ministries vanished beneath the reply envelopes.
lore.legendary: Sir Letterbane broke the wax seal on a decree forbidding birthdays. Every child in the kingdom turned a year older that afternoon, and the king received a terrifyingly large cake.

names.legendary: Luminella, Keeper of Lost Fireflies

lore.common: Comes out of its box in a knot that appears to have qualifications.
lore.uncommon: One bulb goes dark every December and refuses to explain why.
lore.rare: Lures moths into forming patterns that look suspiciously like rude messages.
lore.epic: Climbed every tree in the village overnight and turned the orchard into a galaxy. Astronomers announced a new constellation called The Birthday Tent.
lore.legendary: Luminella gathered the last fireflies of a vanished summer and strung their lights along the winter road. Even now, travellers can follow that gentle glow home.

names.legendary: Sir Smoothbane, Tamer of the Jagged

lore.common: Makes an unbearable scraping sound and insists it is making music.
lore.uncommon: Has a hundred tiny teeth and demands its own toothbrush.
lore.rare: Files the corners off anything it dislikes. The furniture has begun rolling out of the workshop.
lore.epic: Smoothed every stone in the village square overnight. At sunrise the mayor and three carts slid gracefully into the fountain.
lore.legendary: Smoothbane filed the jagged crown of a mountain until even the goats could slide down it. The mountain now charges admission to its winter playground.

names.legendary: Hoserath, Serpent of the Seven Gardens

lore.common: Ties itself in knots whenever the gardener says there isn't time for this. There is never time for this.
lore.uncommon: Squirts directly into its owner's face when they inspect the nozzle. Calls this diagnostics.
lore.rare: Coils itself into a snake shape and scares the cat into learning to fly.
lore.epic: Escaped during the summer fair and washed every car, dog and garden chair in the village. The ducks gave it a medal.
lore.legendary: Hoserath winds beneath seven gardens and drinks from a hidden spring. In drought it rises to water the flowers, but it charges one biscuit per rosebush.

names.legendary: Sir Ironwood, the Impossible Ace

lore.common: Takes a magnificent swing and removes a generous slice of turf. The golf ball watches in disbelief.
lore.uncommon: Digs a perfect little trench where the ball was supposed to be. The groundskeeper is furious.
lore.rare: Sends a hooked shot into the rough and claims it was looking for mushrooms.
lore.epic: Swung so cleanly on the final hole that the ball circled the entire course and returned carrying three lost tees.
lore.legendary: Sir Ironwood once struck a ball across a moonlit valley and into a hole nobody had dug yet. Golfers still search for the green that appeared at dawn.

names.legendary: Teebald, the Tiny King of the First Hole

lore.common: Stands proudly beneath the ball like a tiny royal pedestal, then vanishes into the grass at the first shot.
lore.uncommon: Buries itself in the grass the moment a golfer looks away.
lore.rare: Balances a ball on a needle-thin perch above the rough without touching the ground. Even the caddie is starting to believe in magic.
lore.epic: Sprouted into a miniature tree at the championship, raising the next ball above the golfers' heads.
lore.legendary: Teebald is said to have held the first golf ball ever struck. The ball never returned, and he has spent centuries standing patiently at the same tee.

names.legendary: Guttorius, Keeper of the Roof Sea

lore.common: Eats leaves all autumn, then burps an entire puddle onto the postman's head.
lore.uncommon: Drips directly onto the welcome mat, even when the rest of the street is dry.
lore.rare: Turns itself into a miniature rooftop canal with a fleet of impatient sparrows.
lore.epic: Burst during a storm and sent a waterfall down the front of the town hall. The mayor arrived at work by canoe.
lore.legendary: Guttorius catches every lost raindrop from the oldest roofs in the city. Under full moonlight, his waters reveal the faces of every family that ever lived beneath them.

names.legendary: Serrator, the Unbending Edge

lore.common: Squeaks against a pipe as though it is offended the pipe exists.
lore.uncommon: Bends away from every straight line and calls the resulting squiggle artistic freedom.
lore.rare: Nibbles through a steel bar with its tiny teeth. Then asks for a softer dessert.
lore.epic: Sliced the old town gate into a thousand perfect rings. The blacksmith sold them all as fashionable bracelets.
lore.legendary: Serrator cut a passage through the mountain when every road was buried in winter snow. Its blade grew no duller, though the mountain has held a grudge ever since.

names.legendary: Reelor, Keeper of the Endless Coil

lore.common: Keeps precisely one loop of hose on the patio, directly where you are about to step.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to turn its crank until someone promises not to leave it out all winter.
lore.rare: Reels in the hose while you're still watering. The flowerbed enjoys watching the chase.
lore.epic: Unspooled across an entire neighbourhood, tangling every garden into one vast sprinkler system. The council declared it a water park.
lore.legendary: Reelor wound up the river during a drought and delivered it to thirsty fields one garden at a time. A bewildered fish now lives in its handle.

names.legendary: Cuchulash, Keeper of the Long Puck

lore.common: Flicks the sliotar off the grass before the referee has even blown the whistle.
lore.uncommon: Swings its ashwood head with an echo that sounds suspiciously like a cheering crowd.
lore.rare: Balances the sliotar on its flat blade while sprinting over a rain-soaked field. It never drops a point.
lore.epic: Launched the winning sliotar so far it landed in the rival county's trophy cabinet. Both counties now claim the championship.
lore.legendary: Cuchulash was carved from the last ash tree on an ancient playing field. When its blade strikes, every abandoned hurling pitch rings with the thunder of forgotten finals.

names.legendary: Rimehook, the Mountain's Last Grip

lore.common: Dangles from a wrist strap and taps its owner's knee the entire climb.
lore.uncommon: Clings to the first patch of ice it sees like a puppy refusing to come home.
lore.rare: Bites into a sheer ice wall and holds a climber steady while the mountain shakes.
lore.epic: Anchored a whole rescue party to a frozen waterfall as the mountain rumbled. The waterfall turned into a staircase of ice.
lore.legendary: Rimehook was forged from the first winter's frozen lightning. It hangs beneath the highest summit, waiting to catch the next climber whom the mountain lets fall.

names.legendary: Javelor, the Spear That Found the Stars

lore.common: Flies through the air with great ambition and lands flat with an apologetic thud.
lore.uncommon: Demands the entire throwing field to itself, even when nobody is using it.
lore.rare: Soars beyond the officials' measuring tape and lands with a perfect little bow.
lore.epic: Left the stadium during sports day and returned carrying the winning ribbon from the egg-and-spoon race. Nobody understood the rules any more.
lore.legendary: Javelor crossed seven mountain ranges in a single throw to carry a message to a besieged city. Its silver point is now mounted above the gates that never fell.

names.legendary: Ropearella, Mistress of the Endless Skip

lore.common: Catches a shoelace on the first jump and insists the jumper did it wrong.
lore.uncommon: Sings a skipping rhyme faster and faster until nobody can keep up.
lore.rare: Twirls itself without anyone holding the handles, inviting the shyest child to jump in.
lore.epic: Spun so fast through the school playground that benches, bicycles and the head teacher all began skipping in perfect time.
lore.legendary: Ropearella once turned a rope around an entire village so every child could skip together. When the last child laughed, the rope became a silver circle around the midsummer moon.

names.legendary: Grandmaster Thwack, the Unyielding

lore.common: Yells THUD louder than the kick that hits it. The class appreciates the encouragement.
lore.uncommon: Sidesteps the beginner just enough to make the coach look unfairly nimble.
lore.rare: Absorbs the strongest flying kick and sends the sound bouncing around the gym for an hour.
lore.epic: Took a hundred kicks at the grading, then exploded into a snowstorm of stuffing. Every student earned a white belt for surviving the cleanup.
lore.legendary: Grandmaster Thwack has held its ground against champions from a hundred dojos. Its secret is simple: it never kicks back, but it remembers every foot.

names.legendary: Crossephine, Guardian of the Goal

lore.common: Rocks the ball gently to sleep in its net and drops it the moment the whistle blows.
lore.uncommon: Chooses the worst possible moment to let the ball fall through its strings.
lore.rare: Can catch a flying ball without looking, provided nobody is watching.
lore.epic: Flung a shot so fast that the stadium scoreboard displayed next week's result. The goalkeeper is still searching for the ball.
lore.legendary: Crossephine once caught a falling meteor in its woven pocket and carried it harmlessly over the hills. Its net still glows when the stars come out.

names.legendary: Luxline, Ribbon of the Endless Night

lore.common: Peels off one corner of the wall and dangles like a colourful piece of seaweed.
lore.uncommon: Changes from blue to pink to green whenever someone says they have chosen a colour.
lore.rare: Glows to match its owner's mood, which makes birthday surprises almost impossible.
lore.epic: Turned a sleepy village street into a glowing rainbow runway overnight. The whole neighbourhood arrived in slippers to dance.
lore.legendary: Luxline once wrapped itself around the dark side of the moon, threading light through the craters. Astronauts still see its faint colours when every other lamp has gone out.

names.legendary: Nailhelm, Keeper of the Falling Walls

lore.common: Bends sideways the first time the hammer looks at it. Pretends the angle was planned.
lore.uncommon: Hides point-up on the workshop floor and waits to be discovered by a slipper.
lore.rare: Holds a picture against a wall ten times heavier than it ought to bear. It likes being underestimated.
lore.epic: Refused to let go of a great cathedral mural as the wall crumbled around it. The mural remained hanging in the air until the builders rebuilt the wall beneath it.
lore.legendary: Nailhelm was forged from a shard of the mountain that never moved. When the ancient fortress fell, its last iron nail held the gate aloft until the people escaped.

names.legendary: Nutricus, Last Bolt of the Bridge

lore.common: Rolls straight beneath the heaviest cupboard in the workshop and settles in for a long stay.
lore.uncommon: Strips its own thread so the wrench can spin forever. Thinks this is hilarious.
lore.rare: Clamps onto a loose bolt and refuses to budge even under a giant's spanner.
lore.epic: Locked every bolt in the workshop at once. The machinery stopped, the clocks stalled and the mechanic spent the afternoon negotiating with a little hexagonal tyrant.
lore.legendary: Nutricus held the final bolt of a collapsing bridge while an entire kingdom crossed to safety. When the last traveller reached shore, the tiny iron guardian finally let go.

names.legendary: Rollandra, Painter of the Endless Hall

lore.common: Gives the wall a lovely new colour and the painter's shirt twelve unwanted freckles.
lore.uncommon: Leaves one narrow stripe untouched, no matter how many times it goes over the same spot.
lore.rare: Rolls straight up an impossible wall without a ladder, then waits smugly on the ceiling.
lore.epic: Painted an entire tower before the scaffolding was built, including every startled pigeon perched along its ledges.
lore.legendary: Rollandra covered the endless corridor of the ancient palace with dawn-coloured paint in a single stroke. Travellers who followed the line always found the exit.

names.legendary: Prismaticus, Keeper of the Seventh Hue

lore.common: Grabs the painter's thumb and refuses to let go until it has been praised.
lore.uncommon: Mixes two beautiful colours into a shade best described as disappointed potato.
lore.rare: Discovers an entirely new purple, then forgets how it made it.
lore.epic: Spilled its pigments across the studio and every painting swapped colours. The sea turned orange and the sunsets became startlingly blue.
lore.legendary: Prismaticus kept the seventh hue hidden between two raindrops for centuries. When it finally appeared on a young painter's palette, the rainbow leaned down to demand its missing piece.

names.legendary: Peelix, Finder of Hidden Doors

lore.common: Takes one tiny shaving off the potato and one deeply regretted nick off the chef's knuckle.
lore.uncommon: Makes a single beautiful spiral of apple peel that tangles around the cook's wrist.
lore.rare: Removes the outer layer of anything it touches, including labels, wallpaper and very important envelopes.
lore.epic: Peeled a thousand vegetables in one breath, leaving a mountain of ribbons that wrapped the village square in a crunchy scarf.
lore.legendary: Peelix stripped the moss from an ancient stone wall and found a forgotten door beneath it. Behind the door lay the garden where the first winter apples still grew.

names.legendary: Grumhald, Delver of the Sleeping Stars

lore.common: Hits the only stone in the whole garden and makes the gardener's arms tingle.
lore.uncommon: Strikes sparks off a rock, then pretends it was trying to start a campfire.
lore.rare: Hears mineral veins singing behind solid walls and guides miners to their richest find.
lore.epic: Cracked open a mountain with one strike, revealing a valley of glittering crystals. The tourist board has been insufferable since.
lore.legendary: Grumhald struck the first stone beneath the ancient hills and found a cavern filled with fallen stars. Its blade still hums when the night sky loses one.

names.legendary: Sir Malletmere of the Golden Chukker

lore.common: Is so long that it knocks over a cup of tea before the player even climbs onto the horse.
lore.uncommon: Bends just enough during a swing to send the ball in an unexpected direction.
lore.rare: Strikes with perfect timing at full gallop. The opposing team's horses are demanding a replay.
lore.epic: Sent the winning polo ball soaring over the grandstand and into the royal picnic. The queen awarded a point for style.
lore.legendary: Sir Malletmere scored the deciding goal in a tournament played through a three-day storm. The victory saved the losing kingdom from a terrible tax on horses.

names.legendary: Aquastra, Unmasker of Forgotten Stone

lore.common: Cleans one stripe of patio and leaves the rest looking even worse.
lore.uncommon: Blasts a garden gnome's muddy trousers spotless without asking permission.
lore.rare: Strips centuries of grime from a wall, revealing a very rude medieval doodle.
lore.epic: Unleashed a cleaning wave across the city. Every wall turned dazzling white, including the freshly painted murals and the mayor's beard.
lore.legendary: Aquastra once washed the mud from a buried cathedral and revealed its lost stained-glass doors. The water still carries a thousand years of whispered secrets.

names.legendary: Knockturnus, Champion of the Empty Gym

lore.common: Swings back just in time to bonk the person who hit it.
lore.uncommon: Complains with a loud chain rattle after every punch. It is a terrible sport.
lore.rare: Dodges blows by inches despite having no feet, then swings back with perfect comic timing.
lore.epic: Absorbed a hundred championship punches and returned them as one mighty thud that shook the entire boxing ring.
lore.legendary: Knockturnus trained every great boxer who ever entered the abandoned gym, yet nobody has landed a clean hit. His stitched grin hangs above its door.

names.legendary: Knotticus, Binder of the Seven Seas

lore.common: Ties its own shoelace knot and laughs as the sailor tries to untangle it.
lore.uncommon: Turns one simple loop into a puzzle worthy of the world's most exhausted scout leader.
lore.rare: Winds around a fallen branch and pulls an entire stranded boat back to shore without asking for help.
lore.epic: Joined a tug-of-war between two villages and pulled both teams into the same muddy field. They declared a draw and a new international border.
lore.legendary: Knotticus once tied seven storm winds into a sailor's knot to save a fleet. The knot survives in a bottle; its label says DO NOT UNDO BEFORE SUNDAY.

names.legendary: Ergonaut, Voyager of the Motionless Sea

lore.common: Rows furiously across the living room without moving one centimetre. The carpet is unimpressed.
lore.uncommon: Makes an ocean sound with every pull and occasionally demands a lifebuoy.
lore.rare: Projects the sound of real river water around its user. The gym's fish tank has started answering.
lore.epic: Rowed so aggressively at the fitness centre that every exercise bike began moving backwards. The personal trainer called it a coastal emergency.
lore.legendary: Ergonaut has crossed ten thousand imaginary oceans without leaving the garage. Each crossing produces a real seashell beneath the seat, and nobody knows where they come from.

names.legendary: Helix, the Screw That Holds the Moon

lore.common: Disappears under the sofa seconds before the shelf is ready to assemble.
lore.uncommon: Arrives with a flatpack wardrobe as the mysterious spare piece nobody trusts.
lore.rare: Tightens itself another turn whenever the furniture creaks, making an old chair more stubborn with age.
lore.epic: Loosened one tiny screw in the palace chandelier. It fell harmlessly into the soup, and the royal chef declared it the new garnish.
lore.legendary: Helix holds a silver hinge between the Moon and the night sky. Every time someone forgets a screw during assembly, the Moon wobbles a little in its orbit.

names.legendary: Shedazar the Just-in-Case

lore.common: Hides the garden shears behind eleven empty plant pots, all of which are apparently essential.
lore.uncommon: Opens its sticky door for the cat but slams it whenever someone wants the lawnmower.
lore.rare: Reveals a hidden room of forgotten tools every time a new padlock is fitted.
lore.epic: Sneezed out fifty years of saved wood, tins and bicycle parts onto the lawn. The neighbours discovered they had been missing a greenhouse.
lore.legendary: Shedazar contains an entire kingdom of objects their owners swear may be useful someday. At its centre stands the legendary screw that fits absolutely nothing.

names.legendary: Skipporia, the Rope That Tied the Sky

lore.common: Trips its owner on the very first jump and demands a restart.
lore.uncommon: Twirls so fast that the playground children hear a drumbeat no one is playing.
lore.rare: Can double-under a dozen dancers at once without tangling a single ponytail.
lore.epic: Turned the entire school playground into a skipping contest. Even the benches started bouncing, and the head teacher lost a shoe.
lore.legendary: Skipporia once looped her rope around a falling star and swung it gently back into place. Every leap made beneath her glowing cord steals a moment of weightlessness.

names.legendary: Maulgar, the Mountain's Last Knock

lore.common: Drops onto the workshop floor and sends everyone's teacups bouncing.
lore.uncommon: Demands two hands to lift, then insists the garden wall should be slightly shorter.
lore.rare: Strikes one buried rock so hard that every earthworm nearby receives a polite vibration warning.
lore.epic: Knocked down the old stone wall with one blow, then accidentally opened a forgotten tunnel underneath. The archaeologists arrived before the dust settled.
lore.legendary: Maulgar struck the iron heart of a mountain and awoke its sleeping bell. The sound rolled through valleys for three days, and every stone mason heard their name in it.

names.legendary: Grundle, Digger of the First Path

lore.common: Steals all the neatly cleared snow and dumps it straight into your boots.
lore.uncommon: Insists on moving each scoop twice. Its owner calls this exercise; its owner is wrong.
lore.rare: Flings a packed snowball over three garden fences and into the exact chimney it was aiming for.
lore.epic: Cleared a snowbound stadium by launching the entire pitch of snow into the rival team's car park. The derby was postponed for diplomatic reasons.
lore.legendary: When the village vanished beneath a hundred years of snowfall, Grundle dug a tunnel so long that the children emerged on the first day of spring.

names.legendary: Lumilace, Weaver of a Thousand Nights

lore.common: Sags in the exact middle of every perfectly arranged display.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to blink in rhythm. Its one rebellious bulb is studying jazz.
lore.rare: Calls moths from three gardens away and charges admission in tiny wing scales.
lore.epic: Draped a whole harbour in glowing garlands; the fishing boats followed its lights home through a sea of fog.
lore.legendary: Lumilace tied constellations to a wedding canopy with threads of living light. The stars still gather there on anniversaries to watch the dancing.

names.legendary: Striderax, the Road That Never Moves

lore.common: Counts every step loudly and awards exactly zero points for effort.
lore.uncommon: Speeds up whenever someone tries to step off gracefully.
lore.rare: Runs in the opposite direction to its owner and sends dropped trainers back like angry boomerangs.
lore.epic: Accelerated across the gym so fast that runners from every machine formed a single airborne queue. The yoga teacher called it a new class.
lore.legendary: Striderax was built to carry a wandering giant who had no place left to walk. Its enchanted belt contains a thousand landscapes, yet the giant remains in the same little room listening to rain.

names.legendary: Terraclaw, the Spade of Unborn Gardens

lore.common: Plants bulbs the wrong way up and insists it is an artistic choice.
lore.uncommon: Collects muddy fingerprints on its handle as trophies.
lore.rare: Digs a hole beneath any weed and pulls out the entire root system like a tangled necklace.
lore.epic: Excavated a whole hidden garden overnight, leaving the village green criss-crossed with perfect flower beds and one puzzled cricket team.
lore.legendary: Terraclaw once unearthed a seed sleeping beneath an abandoned city. Its little blade cleared a home for the roots, and flowers eventually climbed every empty window.

names.legendary: Usboria, the Thread Between Worlds

lore.common: Must be flipped over twice before it will fit, even when it is the reversible kind.
lore.uncommon: Tangled itself around three chargers during the night and calls the knot a nest.
lore.rare: Carries forgotten photos through an old computer and returns them with one mysterious extra person in the background.
lore.epic: Knotted every charging cable in the electronics shop into a single writhing hydra. The repair technician requested a sword and a cup of coffee.
lore.legendary: Usboria once connected two ancient machines that spoke different languages, and their first shared message was a lullaby. Since then every lost bit of data dreams of finding its way home through her glowing cord.

names.legendary: Sir Retract, the Seam-Slayer

lore.common: Clicks its blade out to look intimidating, then slides it back in when anyone looks.
lore.uncommon: Lives beneath the tape rolls and only appears once every package is open.
lore.rare: Slices the packing tape without touching the ridiculous amount of bubble wrap underneath.
lore.epic: Opened every crate in the warehouse in one sweep. The shipping labels flew up and rearranged themselves into a very rude poem.
lore.legendary: Cut a single ribbon at the opening of the Great Library, and every locked book in the building unfolded its secrets. It immediately put its blade away.

names.legendary: Vyskar, the Unyielding Grip

lore.common: Nips the woodworker's sleeve when the handle turns one notch too far.
lore.uncommon: Grumbles whenever a crooked plank tries to escape its steel jaws.
lore.rare: Holds a spinning gear perfectly still while its owner gets a cup of tea.
lore.epic: Gripped the workshop bench so tightly during a gale that the entire building blew away around it. The apprentices found their homework still clamped in place.
lore.legendary: Held the final stone of a collapsing bridge while a thousand travellers crossed. When the work was done, it released its grip and the stone turned into a mountain.

names.legendary: Washara, the Ring That Held the Bridge

lore.common: Rolls across the workshop floor whenever its owner bends down to pick it up.
lore.uncommon: Poses as a coin until somebody tries to buy a biscuit with it.
lore.rare: Fits around one stubborn bolt and stops a leak no plumber could explain.
lore.epic: Held the loose bolts of a fairground wheel together while the whole village rode it. The mechanics awarded it a medal shaped exactly like itself.
lore.legendary: A single flat steel ring fastened the final beam of a bridge over the storm river. Centuries later, when the bridge shook, it was still the one piece that would not move.

names.legendary: Ariadne, the Thread That Found Home

lore.common: Rolls beneath the sofa and drags the knitting needles along behind it.
lore.uncommon: Tangles itself into a crown, then appoints the cat royal adviser.
lore.rare: Can knit a picture of a story as someone tells it; pull the thread and the characters briefly step out.
lore.epic: Countess Tanglethorn bound the entire town's lampposts together with one impossible skein. The mayor's parade became a communal skipping game.
lore.legendary: Ariadne unravelled through a labyrinth whose walls moved each night. Her silver thread remembered every turning, guiding the lost children home while the maze quietly tied itself in knots.
